clue.text: Put foot down and went in to drink

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other, here the word for went inside the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
went, in the slang sense of urinated, gives PEED

explanation.surface: A driver floored the accelerator and then popped into a pub for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is the coarse slang sense, to relieve oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting your foot down on the pedal is an idiom for accelerating, going faster.

clue.text: Sort of 23 in place that needs repairing

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so these letters are to be put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A worn-out road junction in some town needs fixing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is CROSSING; the letters of IN PLACE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelican is a British pedestrian crossing with lights the walker controls by button.

clue.text: Supplementary text rambles a bit

indicators.note: a bit means only a piece of the following words is taken, a run of letters spanning them

explanation.surface: A footnote or appendix that goes on a little too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplementary material is additional, added on beyond the main part.

clue.text: Lots meet up after work close to tavern

indicators.note: after places the anagram ahead of the letter that closes the next word
to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters of meet up are reshaped
close to here means the final letter of tavern

explanation.surface: Plenty of people get together at the pub after finishing their shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word meaning a great many, an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Last forward tackles shins now and then

indicators.note: tackles in the sense of grapples with, wrapping around another piece

parts.note: forward in the sense of cheeky or bold gives PERT

indicators.note: now and then picks every other letter of shins, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A rugby forward keeps going for the shins in his tackles from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' and 'forward' look like positions on a team; 'Last' is the verb, to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or endure, to keep going over time.

clue.text: Media story cropped separately — by him?

definitions.text: Media story cropped separately — by him?

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its first and last letters, each trimmed on its own

explanation.surface: Who trims news pieces? The person in charge of a paper, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDIA cropped gives EDI and STORY cropped gives TOR; the whole clue also describes who does the cropping.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's chief is the one who cuts reports to fit, so the clue as a whole describes that role.

clue.text: They show the correct way to initial jobs

parts.note: to initial a document is to sign it
jobs, positions of employment, are posts

explanation.surface: Advice about the proper procedure for approving work by initialling it.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadside markers giving directions show travellers which way to go.

clue.text: Duck eating nothing moped

indicators.note: eating means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: a scoter is a type of sea duck
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A duck refused all food and sulked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moped' looks like the past tense of mope; it is the small motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a light motorcycle, a kind of motor scooter.

clue.text: 23 controllers deal with offal

parts.note: to deal, especially in illegal goods, is to traffic
lights are the lungs of a slaughtered animal, sold as offal

explanation.surface: People in charge of a junction handle animal innards.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals at road junctions govern when vehicles and walkers may go, so they control crossings.

clue.text: It needs some inflation

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is taken, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A remark about a stagnant economy needing a little rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is part of 'inflation', and the whole clue describes a tyre that has gone down.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctured tyre has lost its air and must be pumped up again.

clue.text: Dodge here to find a royal couple in bed?

indicators.note: in puts the royal pieces inside the word for bed

parts.note: a bed of flowers or vegetables is a plot
a pair of royals, R for Rex or Regina, and KING

explanation.surface: Avoid the press here and you might catch the King and Queen in bed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodge' is the American car make, not avoidance.
explanation.definitionFit: An American car park is where a Dodge, a US car brand, would be left.

clue.text: Hydrocarbon, brown, stored in old church

indicators.note: stored in means one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A brown hydrocarbon fuel kept in an old church building.
explanation.definitionFit: Octane is an alkane, a compound of hydrogen and carbon found in petrol.

clue.text: Flags here damage top of hat

indicators.note: damage means the following letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flags down help after a hat is damaged at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' looks like a verb; it means flagstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstones, the paving slabs, are laid along a pavement or walkway.

clue.text: Popular air Mark's forgotten en route

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: forgotten means the letter for mark is left out of the broadcasting word

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast or transmit it
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A hit tune by someone called Mark has slipped from memory while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like a tune; it is the verb, to broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something en route is on the way, during passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Pochard is flying in ecstasy

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters scatter into the air and land in new order

explanation.surface: A pochard duck delights in soaring through the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodic means expressing rapturous delight, being enraptured.

clue.text: Oust American way of speaking around university

indicators.note: around means the American and speech pieces wrap round the letter for university

parts.note: US stands for United States, so American
RP is Received Pronunciation, standard educated British speech

explanation.surface: An American accent pushes out the local one on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp a ruler is to oust them and seize their place.

clue.text: Discard score that's unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word for score is cut off

parts.note: to score a surface is to scrape or scratch it

explanation.surface: Throw away a musical score that was never completed.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap something is to throw it away as no longer wanted.

clue.text: Shelter grouse or last of pheasant

parts.note: to grouse is to complain, to carp

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word pheasant

explanation.surface: A game bird scene: a cover for grouse or a pheasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the game bird; it is the verb, to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: A carport is a roofed shelter for a car, open at the sides.

clue.text: Swears dope is where view is obstructed

parts.note: to blind is to swear, as in effing and blinding
pot is slang for cannabis, also called dope

explanation.surface: A cursing pothead is where the view gets blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind spot is an area a driver or viewer cannot see, hidden from sight.

clue.text: Dash over to watch very famous dancer

indicators.note: over means the word for dash is turned round

parts.note: to dash is to run
to eye something is to watch it

explanation.surface: Rush across to see a very celebrated dancer perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was a celebrated Soviet-born ballet star who defected to the West.

clue.text: Dismissed story, including new sketch

parts.note: a batsman who is dismissed is out

indicators.note: including means the word for story holds the letter for new inside

parts.note: a story, a falsehood, is a lie

explanation.surface: A rejected tale that contains a fresh draft.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing, an outline giving the main shape of something.

clue.text: Welshman ignores a European making aerial

indicators.note: ignores means the A is left out of the Welsh name

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name in crosswords
a Pole is a European, from Poland

explanation.surface: A Welsh fellow snubs a fellow European while building an antenna.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipole is a simple antenna made of two conducting rods.

clue.text: College band entertains old ship making ferry trip?

indicators.note: entertains in the sense of holding a guest, so the band surrounds the old ship letters

parts.note: a ring is a band, as on a finger
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A university band plays aboard a vintage steamer during a ferry trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry journey over a stretch of water is a sea passage from one side to the other.

clue.text: Fine resort is out of bounds

indicators.note: out of bounds means the boundary letters of the resort name are lost

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A seaside town is closed to visitors, which suits someone fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Righto is an informal British way of saying okay, all right.

clue.text: Dope carries on flag here usually

indicators.note: carries means the word for dope holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: dope in the sense of information is gen, British slang
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Cannabis carries on its packet a usual warning flag.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the putting surface typically has a flagstick in the hole.

clue.text: Fit to drive souped-up hot rod way beyond river

indicators.note: souped-up means modified, so these letters and the river letter are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A modified hot rod way past the river is fit for the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle in a safe condition for road use is legally fit to drive.

clue.text: Leave No 10 in bind, reeling

indicators.note: reeling, spinning back, means the whole construction is turned round
in places the numeral inside the word for bind

parts.note: to tie is to bind
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Downing Street is in a fix and staggering after a leave vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 10' suggests Downing Street, the PM's address, but it is the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a place is to make one's departure, to go out.

clue.text: Pedant left out label

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is taken from the word for pedant

parts.note: a stickler insists on exact rules, a pedant

explanation.surface: A fussy person omitted a label.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive label is something stuck on, a gummed tag.

clue.text: Clutching tablet, a goddess approaches

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the goddess wraps round the tablet letter

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A goddess draws near holding a stone tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are ways in, routes or means of approach to something.
